milestones.title: Community Action
milestones.body: Kuruwitu fishers form the Kuruwitu Conservation and Welfare Association (KCWA), later the KCW-CBO.

milestones.title: One of Kenya's Earliest LMMAs
milestones.body: The community closes a 30-ha area from fishing, establishing the Tengefu — one of Kenya's earliest community-driven Locally Managed Marine Areas.

milestones.title: Community Management & Ecological Recovery
milestones.body: Community management with loan schemes, alternative livelihoods, peer visits and data collection. Around 15 years of monitoring shows 400% fish biomass increase, 30% reef recovery, 17% seagrass regrowth (WCS data).

milestones.title: UNDP Equator Prize
milestones.body: The KCW-CBO is awarded the UNDP Equator Prize for community-run marine resource management.

milestones.title: IUCN Blue Champions Award
milestones.body: The KCW-CBO receives the IUCN Blue Champions Award.

milestones.title: Oceans Alive Established
milestones.body: Oceans Alive established as a separate organisation to document, support and share community-led marine conservation.

milestones.title: Supporting Co-Management Development
milestones.body: Support to the development of the Kuruwitu Co-Management Area with the Kuruwitu BMU and government.

milestones.title: First Officially Endorsed CMA
milestones.body: Kuruwitu CMA officially endorsed under the BMU Regulations; Kilifi County BMU Network (17 BMUs) endorsed; first IUCN SAGE analysis in Kenya.

milestones.title: Royal Visit
milestones.body: His Majesty King Charles III visits Kuruwitu and places a coral-restoration unit, drawing international attention to community-led conservation.

milestones.title: Expansion & Partnerships
milestones.body: Expansion to the KAMAMKUKI Joint Co-Management Area and continued partnerships under the 2024–2028 Strategy.
